event_dangdang_toolbox_r1.scene: SETTING on a small patch of grey stone floor, copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): the rat's small wooden hand cart with one big spoked wooden wheel and two long wooden pull handles, and on its bed the SAME old wooden tool box (three of its corners capped with copper plates, the fourth corner only a thin wooden board). event_dangdang_broken_shrine_r1.why: 神像在主圖和 r2 都斷成兩截（無頭身體坐著、頭掉地上）、供盤是棕色木碗；這張變成一整隻完整側躺的石貓、碗變藍白瓷碗。
event_dangdang_broken_shrine_r1.scene: SETTING copied from reference image 3 (the main picture of this same event): a small patch of mossy grey stone floor against a low crumbling grey stone-block wall; the small wooden cat shrine with its dark tiled roof has fallen over and leans crookedly against the wall. The grey stone CAT STATUE is broken into TWO pieces exactly as in reference image 3: its HEADLESS body still sits upright on the floor beside the shrine, and its round stone HEAD lies on the floor right next to the body; the two round eyes of the stone head glow faintly. The round BROWN WOODEN offering bowl lies tipped over on its side on the floor, now empty. Dangdang stands a few steps away from the statue, hugging a big armful of dried fish against his chest with both arms (the fish are held firmly in his arms, none floating). He has frozen in place and shivers: one thin wisp of cold pale-blue mist curls out of the crack of the broken statue, through the air, and sinks into the middle of his chest. He looks down at his own chest with a startled, uneasy face, small shiver lines beside his body and a tiny puff of cold white breath at his mouth.

The bear is covered up to its shoulders by the PATCHWORK QUILT of reference image 3: a quilt sewn from square patches of muted navy blue, dark red and beige, with visible stitched seams; one corner of the quilt is tucked into the straw. Dangdang lies snug in the bear's arm, drowsy and just waking up: half-closed sleepy eyes (both the same), a small resigned face.
